mechanism_narrative: RETAIL_REC has risen for three consecutive weeks (-16.4 to -14.9), indicating a persistent recovery momentum in discretionary shopping and recreation activity that should continue to push RETAIL_REC higher over the next four weeks absent a shock.
evidence_refs: fact:RETAIL_REC rose each week from t-3w to t-0w
failure_condition: Mean RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days is lower than the last 28 days despite three prior weeks of consecutive increase.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp week-on-week drop in WORKPLACES mobility exceeding 20 points below the prior reading signals renewed remote-work or restriction pressure that will suppress weekday commute-linked retail footfall over the following two weeks, pulling RETAIL_REC down.
candidate_trigger: WORKPLACES falls more than 20 points week-on-week (e.g. t-3w to t-2w drop of -7.2 approaches this; a repeat crossing -20 below prior week triggers mechanism)
evidence_refs: fact:WORKPLACES fell from -18.4 to -25.6 between t-3w and t-2w
regime_hint: tightening restrictions or renewed remote work
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC rises over the subsequent two weeks despite a WORKPLACES drop exceeding 20 points week-on-week.

mechanism_narrative: Joint recovery in TRANSIT and WORKPLACES reflects restored commuting and in-person work routines, which together amplify incidental retail visits more than either series alone, driving RETAIL_REC upward over the next four weeks when both rise together.
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT improved from -17.4 to -14.4 between t-2w and t-0w while WORKPLACES recovered from -25.6 to -21.3
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC fails to increase over the next four weeks even when both TRANSIT and WORKPLACES rise simultaneously for two or more consecutive weeks.

mechanism_narrative: A gradual rise in RESIDENTIAL mobility (2.3 to 4.0 over four weeks) indicates increasing time spent at home, consistent with growing caution or habitual homebound behavior during the winter COVID season, which will suppress RETAIL_REC over the next four weeks as people substitute in-person shopping with staying home.
evidence_refs: fact:RESIDENTIAL rose monotonically from 2.3 to 4.0 across the four weeks
regime_hint: winter caution regime with elevated home-staying behavior
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC increases over the next 28 days despite RESIDENTIAL continuing to rise, falsifying the substitution mechanism.

mechanism_narrative: Mid-November timing precedes the Black Friday and pre-Christmas shopping season in Spain, a recurring seasonal pattern that structurally increases retail and recreation visits regardless of other mobility trends, pushing RETAIL_REC higher over the next two to four weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:decision date is 2021-11-15, immediately preceding the Black Friday/holiday shopping period
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC fails to rise in the two weeks surrounding Black Friday despite historically reliable seasonal upticks in this period.

mechanism_narrative: A sudden jump in GROCERY_PHARM above 10 points combined with volatile PARKS readings signals anticipatory stocking behavior ahead of expected new restrictions, which historically precede reduced discretionary RETAIL_REC visits within one week as households preemptively curtail non-essential outings.
candidate_trigger: GROCERY_PHARM exceeds +10 points in a given week (observed at t-1w: 11.0)
evidence_refs: fact:GROCERY_PHARM spiked to 11.0 at t-1w from 5.6 at t-2w
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not decline in the week following a GROCERY_PHARM spike above 10 points, indicating no precautionary stocking linkage.

evidence_refs: fact:PARKS oscillated between 12.9 and -7.1 over the four weeks, showing weather-driven instability
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not rise over the following two weeks even as PARKS mobility trends downward due to seasonal cooling.
